exercise1.prompt: A general escape hatch that is slower than the thing it usually replaces.

hiddenCases.name: the vectorised string methods do the work

exercise1.hint: names.str.strip().str.lower() does both steps to the whole column, and .tolist() hands back plain strings.

questions.prompt: Why is apply usually slower than the vectorised equivalent?
choices: It calls your Python function once per value
questions.explain: The vectorised version does the work once in compiled code; apply pays the Python call overhead for every row.

questions.prompt: When is apply the right tool?
choices: When the logic genuinely has no vectorised form
questions.explain: It is an escape hatch, not a default. Reaching for it first is how people conclude that pandas is slow.

questions.prompt: What does .str give you on a Series?
choices: The text of the whole column
String methods applied to every value
questions.explain: strip, lower, replace, contains and the rest, each running across the whole column at once.
